${\text{mi}}^{2}.$" :question/worked-solution "The exact area of land is ${(\frac{4}{5})}^{2}\,{\text{mi}}^{2}.$

Writing ${(\frac{4}{5})}^{2}$ with multiplication signs, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\frac{4}{5})}^{2} & ={{\frac{4}{5}\times \frac{4}{5}}_{⏟}}_{2\text{ times}} \\  & =\frac{4\times 4}{5\times 5} \\  & =\frac{16}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{(\frac{4}{5})}^{2}=\frac{16}{25}.
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-40a52d3e-493d-5f72-b1e1-ef146d9e54e7"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-40a52d3e-493d-5f72-b1e1-ef146d9e54e7" :answer-field/id #uuid "40a52d3e-493d-5f72-b1e1-ef146d9e54e7" :answer-field/key "field-1" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank :answer-field/correct "answer-47cde53f-47d7-5ae4-8572-e9ac9bf6754d" :answer-field/choices ["answer-47cde53f-47d7-5ae4-8572-e9ac9bf6754d"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-47cde53f-47d7-5ae4-8572-e9ac9bf6754d" :answer/id #uuid "47cde53f-47d7-5ae4-8572-e9ac9bf6754d" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{16}{25}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186054858 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-215d1b37-57d3-50ad-9730-b954c879d087"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id "question-215d1b37-57d3-50ad-9730-b954c879d087" :question/id #uuid "215d1b37-57d3-50ad-9730-b954c879d087" :question/math-academy-id "q-166798" :question/problem "Building company policy states that each ton of cement mixture should contain at least $0.7$ tons of sand. tons of sand in $1.2$ tons of cement mixture." :question/worked-solution "To determine how much sand is in $1.2$ tons of the cement mixture, we have to multiply $1.2$ by $0.7.$

We proceed by multiplying the two numbers just as we would with whole numbers.

Notice that the second number has a leading $0$, which we ignore during the multiplication:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \begin{aligned} &  & \,\,\,\,\,\begin{aligned} \\ 1\end{aligned}\,\,\,\, &  \\  &  & \,\,\,\,1\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,.2\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,\times \,\,\,\, &  & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,.7\,\,\,\, \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,8\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,4\,\,\,\,\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

We now count the total number of decimal places in the two factors.

There is $1$ decimal place in $1.2$ and there is $1$ decimal place in $0.7.$
Therefore, their product will have $1+1=2$ decimal places.

So, we take our value of $84$ and add a decimal point to make a number with $2$ decimal places.

$$
\,\overset{↓}{.}\,\,\,{{84}_{⏟}}_{2\text{ digits}}
$$

Hence, $1.2\times 0.7=0.84.$

We conclude that there are $0.84$ tons of sand in $1.2$ tons of the cement mixture." :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-a95f5153-0f06-5465-8815-86cb9c85319c"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-a95f5153-0f06-5465-8815-86cb9c85319c" :answer-field/id #uuid "a95f5153-0f06-5465-8815-86cb9c85319c" :answer-field/key "field-1" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank :answer-field/correct "answer-8d1c2dc7-edf8-570a-812f-d15c687b21fd" :answer-field/choices ["answer-8d1c2dc7-edf8-570a-812f-d15c687b21fd"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-8d1c2dc7-edf8-570a-812f-d15c687b21fd" :answer/id #uuid "8d1c2dc7-edf8-570a-812f-d15c687b21fd" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "0.84" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186138368 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-6535052d-d80b-57f3-9a80-25b64c4c2047"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id "question-6535052d-d80b-57f3-9a80-25b64c4c2047" :question/id #uuid "6535052d-d80b-57f3-9a80-25b64c4c2047" :question/math-academy-id "q-166799" :question/problem "The building company combines $1.6$ tons of sand with $0.69$ tons of cement to make their cement mixture. tons." :question/worked-solution "To find the total weight of the mixture, we need to calculate the sum $1.6+0.69.$

There is $1$ decimal place in $1.6$ and $2$ decimal places in $0.69.$

To add the numbers, they both need to have the same number of decimals. Hence, we rewrite the first number so that it has $2$ decimal places:

$$
1.6=1.60
$$

Next, we line up the decimal points:

$$
\begin{aligned} &  & \,\,\,\,1\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,6\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,+\,\,\,\, &  & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,6\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,9\,\,\,\, \\  &  &  & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, &  & \end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we proceed by adding the two numbers just as we would with whole numbers:

$$
\begin{aligned} &  & \,\,\,\,\begin{aligned} \\ 1\end{aligned}\,\,\,\, &  &  \\  &  & \,\,\,\,1\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,6\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,+\,\,\,\, &  & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,6\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,9\,\,\,\, \\  &  & \,\,\,\,2\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,2\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,9\,\,\,\,\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the total weight of the mixture is $2.29$ tons." :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-02e8ab80-f28a-5a91-a4ee-5bbed7cc0309"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-02e8ab80-f28a-5a91-a4ee-5bbed7cc0309" :answer-field/id #uuid "02e8ab80-f28a-5a91-a4ee-5bbed7cc0309" :answer-field/key "field-1" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank :answer-field/correct "answer-b46221bb-c9ba-5b3b-af2a-aefe7602f145" :answer-field/choices ["answer-b46221bb-c9ba-5b3b-af2a-aefe7602f145"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-b46221bb-c9ba-5b3b-af2a-aefe7602f145" :answer/id #uuid "b46221bb-c9ba-5b3b-af2a-aefe7602f145" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2.29" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186054862 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-ee99225f-5b1d-5184-84fe-979d439fc52f"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id "question-ee99225f-5b1d-5184-84fe-979d439fc52f" :question/id #uuid "ee99225f-5b1d-5184-84fe-979d439fc52f" :question/math-academy-id "q-166800" :question/problem "Of the cement mixture prepared, $1.87$ tons were used to construct the houses. tons of cement mixture are left over." :question/worked-solution "In part 3, we found that the company prepared $2.29$ tons of cement mixture.

To determine the amount of cement mixture remaining, we need to calculate $2.29-1.87.$

First, we line up the decimal points:

$$
\begin{aligned} &  & \,\,\,\,2\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,2\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,9\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,-\,\,\,\, &  & \,\,\,\,1\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,8\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,7\,\,\,\, \\  &  &  & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, &  & \end{aligned}
$$

Next, we proceed by subtracting the two numbers just as we would with whole numbers:

$$
\begin{aligned} &  & \,\,\,\,\,\begin{aligned} \\ 1\end{aligned}\,\,\,\, &  & \,\,\,\,\,\begin{aligned} \\ 12\end{aligned}\,\,\,\, &  \\  &  & \,\,\,\,2\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,2\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,9\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,-\,\,\,\, &  & \,\,\,\,1\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,8\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,7\,\,\,\, \\  &  & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,4\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,2\,\,\,\,\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $0.42$ tons of cement mixture are left over." :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-f34c47c7-21ad-5287-bc9c-731eacee1cb5"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-f34c47c7-21ad-5287-bc9c-731eacee1cb5" :answer-field/id #uuid "f34c47c7-21ad-5287-bc9c-731eacee1cb5" :answer-field/key "field-1" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank :answer-field/correct "answer-bcf24fbb-54b2-594a-834d-965cf812e613" :answer-field/choices ["answer-bcf24fbb-54b2-594a-834d-965cf812e613"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-bcf24fbb-54b2-594a-834d-965cf812e613" :answer/id #uuid "bcf24fbb-54b2-594a-834d-965cf812e613" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "0.42" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186073705 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-ecc24b66-1c17-5f12-9e7e-a64bd2e2d9c8"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id "question-ecc24b66-1c17-5f12-9e7e-a64bd2e2d9c8" :question/id #uuid "ecc24b66-1c17-5f12-9e7e-a64bd2e2d9c8" :question/math-academy-id "q-166801" :question/problem "One of the workers cuts $3\,\frac{3}{4}\,\text{ft}$ from a pipe measuring $5\,\frac{1}{8}\,\text{ft}.$ What is the length of the remaining pipe? Express your answer as a mixed number.

The length of the remaining pipe is$\,$
{{field-1}}
$\text{ft}.$" :question/worked-solution "The length of the remaining pipe is $(5\,\frac{1}{8}-3\,\frac{3}{4})\text{ft}.$

Writing $5\,\frac{1}{8}$ as an improper fraction, we have

$$
5\,\frac{1}{8}=\frac{5\times 8+1}{8}=\frac{41}{8}.
$$

Writing $3\,\frac{3}{4}$ as an improper fraction, we have

$$
3\,\frac{3}{4}=\frac{3\times 4+3}{4}=\frac{15}{4}.
$$

Therefore, our problem now is to work out the following:

$$
\frac{41}{8}-\frac{15}{4}
$$

To subtract two fractions with unlike denominators, we need to express each fraction as an equivalent fraction with a common denominator.

In this question, we can make a common denominator of $8.$

To put $\frac{15}{4}$ over a denominator of $8,$ we multiply the numerator and denominator by $2:$

$$
\frac{15}{4}=\frac{15\times 2}{4\times 2}=\frac{30}{8}
$$

We can now subtract the fractions. We keep the denominator the same, and we subtract the numerators:

$$
\frac{41}{8}-\frac{30}{8}=\frac{11}{8}
$$

Finally, we convert back to a mixed number:

$$
\frac{11}{8}=1\,\text{R}\,3=1\,\frac{3}{8}
$$

Therefore, $1\,\frac{3}{8}\,\text{ft}$ of pipe remains." :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-89b6a21c-a813-55f9-b362-1ae1f8cff07b"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-89b6a21c-a813-55f9-b362-1ae1f8cff07b" :answer-field/id #uuid "89b6a21c-a813-55f9-b362-1ae1f8cff07b" :answer-field/key "field-1" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank :answer-field/correct "answer-dda3fa24-a3e1-52ae-b9a9-bebd3842e781" :answer-field/choices ["answer-dda3fa24-a3e1-52ae-b9a9-bebd3842e781"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-dda3fa24-a3e1-52ae-b9a9-bebd3842e781" :answer/id #uuid "dda3fa24-a3e1-52ae-b9a9-bebd3842e781" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "1\,\frac{3}{8}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186073676 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-1e21dfbe-7205-50ca-b839-4d1dcb287bbd"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id "question-1e21dfbe-7205-50ca-b839-4d1dcb287bbd" :question/id #uuid "1e21dfbe-7205-50ca-b839-4d1dcb287bbd" :question/math-academy-id "q-166802" :question/problem "The company used $104.7\,\text{ft}$ of piping to construct $5$ identical houses. $2x - y = 5y - z.$" :question/worked-solution "We need to isolate $x,$ so we will treat the other variables $y$ and $z$ as constants. We can use the addition and multiplication principles to solve for $x.$

First, we add $y$ to both sides:

$$
\eqalign{
		2x - y &= 5y - z \[5pt]
		2x - y + y &= 5y - z + y \[5pt]
		2x &= 6y - z
	}
$$

 

Then, we divide both sides by $2\mathbin{:}$

$$
\eqalign{
		2x &= 6y - z \[5pt]
		\dfrac {2x} 2 &= \dfrac{6y - z} {2} \[5pt]
		x &= \dfrac{6y - z} {2}
	}
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186064194 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-14cd0a28-442e-5455-9aaf-cc966e4aa8e5" "question-237b013e-fcd6-5777-9bce-b39ac50c9f8e"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id 17592186063970 :question/worked-solution "We need to isolate $m,$ so we will treat the other variables $E$ and $C$ as constants. Since $m$ is being multiplied by $C,$ we need to divide both sides of the equation by $C$:
![](images/27/27683350a3eb25bd3962e12724a01f09350d4c62ba85afb137df8cff27992be7.svg)
Thus, $m = \dfrac E C.$

**Note:** This result assumes that $C\neq 0.$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186064195 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-de5d5814-9f69-514d-a764-4ee1edcf544a" "question-220b7284-89df-58d8-b7fb-14c6a632a4f4"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id 17592186063971 :question/problem "The total energy $E$ of a body moving with a (squared) velocity $V$ can be approximated using the equation $E = mC + \dfrac{1}{2}mV.$ Find an expression for $V$ in terms of the other quantities." :question/worked-solution "We need to isolate $V,$ so we will treat the other variables $E,$ $C,$ and $m$ as constants. We can use the addition and multiplication principles to solve for $V.$

First, we subtract $mC$ from both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}E & =mC+\frac{1}{2}mV \\ E-mC & =mC+\frac{1}{2}mV-mC \\ E-mC & =\frac{1}{2}mV\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we multiply by $2$ to get rid of the fraction:

$$
\begin{aligned}E-mC & =\frac{1}{2}mV \\ 2\cdot (E-mC) & =2\cdot \frac{1}{2}mV \\ 2(E-mC) & =mV\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide by $m$ to get $V$ alone:

$$
\begin{aligned}2(E-mC) & =mV \\ \frac{2(E-mC)}{m} & =\frac{mV}{m} \\ \frac{2(E-mC)}{m} & =V\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $V = \dfrac{2(E-mC)}{m}.$

**Note:** This result assumes that $m\neq 0.$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "question-16ef2d7f-f052-5e96-9861-83b3cce4c0bd" :question/id #uuid "16ef2d7f-f052-5e96-9861-83b3cce4c0bd" :question/math-academy-id "q-6272" :question/problem "Solve for $a$ where $c=3a+7b.$" :question/worked-solution "We need to isolate $a,$ so we will treat the other variables $b$ and $c$ constants. We can use the addition and multiplication principles to solve for $a.$

First, we subtract $7b$ from both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =3a+7b \\ c-7b & =3a+7b-7b \\ c-7b & =3a\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide both sides by $3:$

$$

First, we subtract $2xz$ from both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}2xz-3y & =4w \\ 2xz-3y-2xz & =4w-2xz \\ -3y & =4w-2xz\end{aligned}

$$
E=PQ-C,
$$

where $P$ is the sale price of a good, $Q$ is the number of goods sold, and $C$ is the cost of producing $Q$ goods. 

What is the formula for the price in terms of the other variables?" :question/worked-solution "We need to isolate $P,$ so we will treat the other variables $E,$ $Q,$ and $C$ as constants. We can use the addition and multiplication principles to solve for $P.$

First, we add $C$ to both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}E & =PQ-C \\ E+C & =PQ-C+C \\ E+C & =PQ\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide by $Q$ to get $P$ alone:

$$
\begin{aligned}E+C & =PQ \\ \frac{E+C}{Q} & =\frac{PQ}{Q} \\ \frac{E+C}{Q} & =P\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $P=\frac{E+C}{Q}.$

**Note:** This result assumes that $Q\ne 0.$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-7599f77d-da1f-5c75-baeb-b3ad971719bd"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-7599f77d-da1f-5c75-baeb-b3ad971719bd" :answer-field/id #uuid "7599f77d-da1f-5c75-baeb-b3ad971719bd" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-65f5c1ef-d90e-568c-bb69-d1d84bbf05ac" :answer-field/choices ["answer-0776833c-e0c2-532d-b051-2d003c8e095a" "answer-39705b79-f9e1-5882-96bb-64867d45e168" "answer-65f5c1ef-d90e-568c-bb69-d1d84bbf05ac" "answer-b9a6184b-cc9c-5368-98bb-fcc102c67792" "answer-c8133753-993a-528a-abab-a54fb3d9628e"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-0776833c-e0c2-532d-b051-2d003c8e095a" :answer/id #uuid "0776833c-e0c2-532d-b051-2d003c8e095a" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "C=PQ-E" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-39705b79-f9e1-5882-96bb-64867d45e168" :answer/id #uuid "39705b79-f9e1-5882-96bb-64867d45e168" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "P=Q(E+C)" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-65f5c1ef-d90e-568c-bb69-d1d84bbf05ac" :answer/id #uuid "65f5c1ef-d90e-568c-bb69-d1d84bbf05ac" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "P=\frac{E+C}{Q}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-b9a6184b-cc9c-5368-98bb-fcc102c67792" :answer/id #uuid "b9a6184b-cc9c-5368-98bb-fcc102c67792" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "P=\frac{E-C}{Q}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-c8133753-993a-528a-abab-a54fb3d9628e" :answer/id #uuid "c8133753-993a-528a-abab-a54fb3d9628e" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "Q=\frac{E+C}{P}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186065434 :tutorial/content "Sometimes we might be given an equation that contains more than one variable and asked to isolate one of the variables. This means that we need to put the variable we're interested in on one side of the equation (on its own) and everything else on the other.

For example, suppose we want to isolate $n$ in the equation

$$
2n - k = q + 5k.
$$

The equation has three variables, $n,$ $k,$ and $q.$ However, we will treat the variables $k$ and $q$ as constants because we are solving for $n$ only. We can use the addition and multiplication principles to solve for $n\mathbin{.}$ 

First, we add $k$ to both sides:

$$
\eqalign{
		2n - k &= q + 5k \[5pt]
		2n - k + k &= q + 5k +k \[5pt]
		2n &= q + 6k \
	}
$$

 

Then, we divide both sides of the equation by $2\mathbin{:}$

$$
\eqalign{
		2n &= q + 6k \[5pt]

In the reduced matrix above, the pivot columns correspond to the linearly independent vectors ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ that form the basis of our span.

Since the acceleration of the particle $P$ is $4x\,{m/s}^{2},$ we have 

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=4x.
$$

Using the fact that

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}),
$$

we can rewrite our equation as

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})=4x.
$$

Integrating both sides of the above equation with respect to $x,$ we have

$$
\int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})\text{d}x=\int 4x\,\text{d}x
$$

which gives the general solution

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}=2{x}^{2}+C.
$$

Now, since $v=2\sqrt{3}\,m/s$ when $x=2\sqrt{2}\,m,$ we can find the value of the constant $C,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & =2{x}^{2}+C \\ \frac{1}{2}(2\sqrt{3})^{2} & =2(2\sqrt{2})^{2}+C \\ C & =6-16 \\ C & =-10\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}=2{x}^{2}-10.
$$

Finally, the particle is instantaneously at rest when $v(x)=0\,m/s.$ We find the displacement of the particle when instantaneously at rest by substituting $v=0$ in the equation above and solving for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & =2{x}^{2}-10 \\ \frac{1}{2}(0)^{2} & =2{x}^{2}-10 \\ 2{x}^{2} & =10 \\ {x}^{2} & =5 \\ x & =\pm \sqrt{5}\,m\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-748a88b6-3bf6-5b57-aacf-5ce371f8acba"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-748a88b6-3bf6-5b57-aacf-5ce371f8acba" :answer-field/id #uuid "748a88b6-3bf6-5b57-aacf-5ce371f8acba" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-acbb534e-c48b-5374-b024-0f4966f54ecd" :answer-field/choices ["answer-f502dce3-880c-5ad9-9d68-43c719b39205" "answer-6cf5d513-6835-539d-a925-f3dbf75e5b3d" "answer-7b71dd8f-bac1-5c10-8567-8f83b147a02c" "answer-acbb534e-c48b-5374-b024-0f4966f54ecd" "answer-1499bde2-2ab6-5730-a6dc-62d7a289a0d9"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-f502dce3-880c-5ad9-9d68-43c719b39205" :answer/id #uuid "f502dce3-880c-5ad9-9d68-43c719b39205" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "x=5\,m" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-6cf5d513-6835-539d-a925-f3dbf75e5b3d" :answer/id #uuid "6cf5d513-6835-539d-a925-f3dbf75e5b3d" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "x=\pm 2\,m" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-7b71dd8f-bac1-5c10-8567-8f83b147a02c" :answer/id #uuid "7b71dd8f-bac1-5c10-8567-8f83b147a02c" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "x=\pm 3\sqrt{2}\,m" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-acbb534e-c48b-5374-b024-0f4966f54ecd" :answer/id #uuid "acbb534e-c48b-5374-b024-0f4966f54ecd" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "x=\pm \sqrt{5}\,m" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-1499bde2-2ab6-5730-a6dc-62d7a289a0d9" :answer/id #uuid "1499bde2-2ab6-5730-a6dc-62d7a289a0d9" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "x=\sqrt{3}\,m" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-bf4a1221-96ce-539b-bfe1-3711516162e7" :question/id #uuid "bf4a1221-96ce-539b-bfe1-3711516162e7" :question/math-academy-id "q-163580" :question/problem "A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis. When the displacement of $P$ from the origin is $x\,m,$ the velocity is $v\,m/s,$ and the acceleration is $(2x-3)\,{m/s}^{2}.$ If $P$ has velocity $2\,m/s$ when its displacement is $3\,m,$ find the values of $x$ for which $P$ is instantaneously at rest." :question/worked-solution "![](images/ca/ca6267f534b9cad9bc1646eef473d85aab1ba6a5f4738b8212b107b753ea2381.png)

Since the acceleration of the particle $P$ is $(2x-3)\,{m/s}^{2},$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=2x-3.
$$

Using the fact that

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}),
$$

we can rewrite our equation as

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})=2x-3.
$$

Integrating both sides of the above equation with respect to $x,$ we have

$$
\int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})\text{d}x=\int (2x-3)\,\text{d}x
$$

which gives the general solution

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}={x}^{2}-3x+C.
$$

Now, since $v=2\,m/s$ when $x=3\,m,$ we can find the value of the constant $C,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & ={x}^{2}-3x+C \\ \frac{1}{2}(2)^{2} & =(3)^{2}-3(3)+C \\ C & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}={x}^{2}-3x+2.
$$

Finally, the particle is instantaneously at rest when $v(x)=0\,m/s.$ We find the displacement of the particle when instantaneously at rest by substituting $v=0$ in the equation above and solving for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & ={x}^{2}-3x+2 \\ \frac{1}{2}(0)^{2} & ={x}^{2}-3x+2 \\ {x}^{2}-3x+2 & =0 \\ (x-1)(x-2) & =0 \\ x & =1\,m,\,2\,m.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-c6154e74-64bf-5093-bf56-6eed3e0fc3f3"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-c6154e74-64bf-5093-bf56-6eed3e0fc3f3" :answer-field/id #uuid "c6154e74-64bf-5093-bf56-6eed3e0fc3f3" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-a0e376fc-17af-5815-b320-dee9d3fc6efe" :answer-field/choices ["answer-aadde328-0a84-557d-ab82-907dd5467e85" "answer-b99f81d8-cedc-552f-8e21-52c06f6a9822" "answer-69d48d35-eeeb-5306-96d0-da006a058aed" "answer-a0e376fc-17af-5815-b320-dee9d3fc6efe" "answer-c561cd7c-8f01-53ea-a88e-1356c8d77c5e"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-aadde328-0a84-557d-ab82-907dd5467e85" :answer/id #uuid "aadde328-0a84-557d-ab82-907dd5467e85" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "x=1\,m" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-b99f81d8-cedc-552f-8e21-52c06f6a9822" :answer/id #uuid "b99f81d8-cedc-552f-8e21-52c06f6a9822" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "x=4\,m" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-69d48d35-eeeb-5306-96d0-da006a058aed" :answer/id #uuid "69d48d35-eeeb-5306-96d0-da006a058aed" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "x=5\,m" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-a0e376fc-17af-5815-b320-dee9d3fc6efe" :answer/id #uuid "a0e376fc-17af-5815-b320-dee9d3fc6efe" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "$x=1\,m$ and $x=2\,m$" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-c561cd7c-8f01-53ea-a88e-1356c8d77c5e" :answer/id #uuid "c561cd7c-8f01-53ea-a88e-1356c8d77c5e" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "$x=2\,m$ and $x=5\,m$" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-f72c0da0-a5f4-5e3b-8c36-5827ed531170" :question/id #uuid "f72c0da0-a5f4-5e3b-8c36-5827ed531170" :question/math-academy-id "q-163556" :question/problem "A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis. When the displacement of $P$ from the origin is $x\,m,$ the velocity is $v\,m/s,$ and the acceleration is $(3+kx)\,{m/s}^{2},$ where $k$ is a positive constant. If $P$ has velocity $v=8\,m/s$ at the origin and the particle has velocity $v=8\sqrt{2}\,m/s$ when its displacement is $8\,m,$ find the value of $k.$" :question/worked-solution "![](images/f3/f368d2de12462a1790322edca188232bf8fafe3951facdb29b334e285807b9fe.png)

Since the acceleration of the particle $P$ is $(3+kx)\,{m/s}^{2},$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=3+kx.
$$

Using the fact that

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}),
$$

we can rewrite our equation as

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})=3+kx.
$$

Integrating both sides of the above equation with respect to $x,$ we have

$$
\int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})\text{d}x=\int (3+kx)\,\text{d}x
$$

which gives the general solution

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}=3x+\frac{k{x}^{2}}{2}+C.
$$

Now, since $v=8\,m/s$ when $x=0\,m,$ we can find the value of the constant $C,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & =3x+\frac{k{x}^{2}}{2}+C \\ \frac{1}{2}(8)^{2} & =3(0)+\frac{k(0)^{2}}{2}+C \\ C & =32\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}=3x+\frac{k{x}^{2}}{2}+32.
$$

Finally, since $v=8\sqrt{2}\,m/s$ when $x=8\,m,$ we can find the value of the positive constant $k,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & =3x+\frac{k{x}^{2}}{2}+32 \\ \frac{1}{2}(8\sqrt{2})^{2} & =3(8)+\frac{k(8)^{2}}{2}+32 \\ 64 & =24+32k+32 \\ 32k & =8 \\ k & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-6c0cd56a-fac1-59c9-9082-8dcbbdf2dead"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-6c0cd56a-fac1-59c9-9082-8dcbbdf2dead" :answer-field/id #uuid "6c0cd56a-fac1-59c9-9082-8dcbbdf2dead" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-93f5f517-1af6-5399-a4d2-94637bc4642f" :answer-field/choices ["answer-77c1c959-8901-5fd3-bde1-0be7a13d7921" "answer-d60b1661-414b-525a-a604-03b55bb6095a" "answer-93f5f517-1af6-5399-a4d2-94637bc4642f" "answer-a61b1f2d-1d39-5240-aeb9-34d945752a5c" "answer-1ad4a456-d983-59d9-aa10-433b9a7fb149"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-77c1c959-8901-5fd3-bde1-0be7a13d7921" :answer/id #uuid "77c1c959-8901-5fd3-bde1-0be7a13d7921" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-d60b1661-414b-525a-a604-03b55bb6095a" :answer/id #uuid "d60b1661-414b-525a-a604-03b55bb6095a" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "4" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-93f5f517-1af6-5399-a4d2-94637bc4642f" :answer/id #uuid "93f5f517-1af6-5399-a4d2-94637bc4642f" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{4}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-a61b1f2d-1d39-5240-aeb9-34d945752a5c" :answer/id #uuid "a61b1f2d-1d39-5240-aeb9-34d945752a5c" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{3}{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-1ad4a456-d983-59d9-aa10-433b9a7fb149" :answer/id #uuid "1ad4a456-d983-59d9-aa10-433b9a7fb149" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{4}{3}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-e3dde6ce-080b-590e-80f0-4c60a929946f" :question/id #uuid "e3dde6ce-080b-590e-80f0-4c60a929946f" :question/math-academy-id "q-163547" :question/problem "A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis. When the displacement of $P$ from the origin is $x\,m,$ the velocity is $v\,m/s,$ the magnitude of the acceleration is $k{x}^{3}\,{m/s}^{2},$ where $k$ is a positive constant, and the acceleration is directed toward $O.$ If $P$ has velocity $v=8\sqrt{17}\,m/s$ at the origin and the particle has a velocity of $v=8\,m/s$ when its displacement is $4\,m,$ find the value of $k.$" :question/worked-solution "![](images/f3/f3879ccc6084d9a0ef8bef2e211e2e7fd9dcc811fb04f06c2ef7429e4d574871.png)

Since the acceleration of the particle $P$ has magnitude $k{x}^{3}\,{m/s}^{2}$ and is directed *toward* $O,$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=-k{x}^{3}.
$$

Using the fact that

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}),
$$

we can rewrite our equation as

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})=-k{x}^{3}.
$$

Integrating both sides of the above equation with respect to $x,$ we have

$$
\int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})\text{d}x=\int (-k{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x
$$

which gives the general solution

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}=-\frac{k}{4}{x}^{4}+C.
$$

Now, since $v=8\sqrt{17}\,m/s$ when $x=0\,m,$ we can find the value of the constant $C,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & =-\frac{k}{4}{x}^{4}+C \\ \frac{1}{2}(8\sqrt{17})^{2} & =-\frac{k}{4}(0)^{4}+C \\ C & =544\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}=544-\frac{k}{4}{x}^{4}.
$$

Finally, since $v=8\,m/s$ when $x=4\,m,$ we can find the value of the positive constant $k,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & =544-\frac{k}{4}{x}^{4} \\ \frac{1}{2}(8)^{2} & =544-\frac{k}{4}(4)^{4} \\ 32 & =544-64k \\ 64k & =512 \\ k & =8.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-efd9e216-e266-5141-b8bb-3d95bb41fe42"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id a positive constant. If $P$ has velocity $v=2\,m/s$ at the origin and the particle has velocity $v=8\,m/s$ when its displacement is $8\,m,$ find the value of $k.$" :question/worked-solution "![](images/77/771929267e75b5d45b9777399c784fafc570386834eee6738fead9ff1bb78e5e.png)

Since the acceleration of the particle $P$ is $k\sqrt[3]{x}\,{m/s}^{2},$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=k\sqrt[3]{x}.
$$

Using the fact that

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}),
$$

we can rewrite our equation as

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})=k\sqrt[3]{x}.
$$

Integrating both sides of the above equation with respect to $x,$ we have

$$
\int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})\text{d}x=\int k\sqrt[3]{x}\,\text{d}x
$$

which gives the general solution

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}=\frac{3k}{4}{x}^{4/3}+C.
$$

Now, since $v=2\,m/s$ when $x=0\,m,$ we can find the value of the constant $C,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & =\frac{3k}{4}{x}^{4/3}+C \\ \frac{1}{2}(2)^{2} & =\frac{3k}{4}(0)^{4/3}+C \\ C & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}=\frac{3k}{4}{x}^{4/3}+2.
$$

Finally, since $v=8\,m/s$ when $x=8\,m,$ we can find the value of the positive constant $k,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & =\frac{3k}{4}{x}^{4/3}+2 \\ \frac{1}{2}(8)^{2} & =\frac{3k}{4}(8)^{4/3}+2 \\ 32 & =12k+2 \\ 12k & =30 \\ k & =\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-c645bc4d-e925-5887-895a-ddac573c52dd"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "question-5fda4f28-bb84-514e-9e1c-0feb53f5b922" :question/id #uuid "5fda4f28-bb84-514e-9e1c-0feb53f5b922" :question/math-academy-id "q-163554" :question/problem "A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis in the direction of increasing $x$ where $x\ge 0.$ When the displacement of $P$ from the origin is $x\,m,$ the velocity is $v\,m/s,$ and the acceleration is $(7-x)\,{m/s}^{2}.$ If $P$ has velocity $v=\sqrt{6}\,m/s$ at the origin, find the maximum velocity of the particle." :question/worked-solution "![](images/51/51ccc6e3e341931c7a244c4617ede78f901478487589f9023b16c3dae80ebc62.png)

The extrema of the velocity occur at the critical points of $v.$ Since the acceleration of the particle $P$ is $(7-x)\,{m/s}^{2},$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=7-x.
$$

To find the moments where $v$ is a maximum, we need to solve $\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=0$ and test each solution using the first or second derivative test.

Solving $\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=0$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}7-x & =0 \\ x & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the extremum of the velocity function occurs when $x=7\,m.$

We now test the extreme value using the first derivative test. We summarize the necessary information in a table, shown below.

| $x$ | $(0,7)$ | $7$ | $(7,\infty )$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Test Point | $6$ |  | $8$ |
| $\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}$ | $1>0$ | $0$ | $-1<0$ |
| $v$ | $↗$ | max | $↘$ |

We conclude that the velocity is maximized when $x=7\,m.$

Next, using the fact that

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}),
$$

we can rewrite our initial equation as

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})=7-x.
$$

Integrating both sides of the above equation with respect to $x,$ we have

$$
\int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})\text{d}x=\int (7-x)\,\text{d}x
$$

which gives the general solution

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}=7x-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+C.
$$

Now, since $v=\sqrt{6}\,m/s$ when $x=0\,m,$ we can find the value of the constant $C,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & =7x-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+C \\ \frac{1}{2}(\sqrt{6})^{2} & =7(0)-\frac{1}{2}(0)^{2}+C \\ C & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & =7x-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+3 \\ {v}^{2} & =14x-{x}^{2}+6 \\ v & =\pm \sqrt{-{x}^{2}+14x+6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the particle is moving in the direction of increasing $x,$ we have that $v(x)>0,$ so we can disregard the negative square root. Therefore,

$$
v(x)=\sqrt{-{x}^{2}+14x+6}.
$$

Finally, we calculate the maximum velocity:

$$
{v}_{max}=v(7)=\sqrt{-(7)^{2}+14(7)+6}=\sqrt{55}\,m/s
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-561bb6d9-fdfa-583e-add7-ec5538f0b8c0"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-561bb6d9-fdfa-583e-add7-ec5538f0b8c0" :answer-field/id #uuid "561bb6d9-fdfa-583e-add7-ec5538f0b8c0" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-52f39f9c-16d0-5e71-b870-45274fd72ab1" :answer-field/choices ["answer-330011e7-cec4-558b-83ce-0451e10c41da" "answer-70c5036d-e847-5a0e-bf6c-48538005df98" "answer-7e188a6e-5859-50df-8694-4924096a1526" "answer-52f39f9c-16d0-5e71-b870-45274fd72ab1" "answer-dd5d7801-28ac-5ea0-88d2-5bd0cb858a80"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-330011e7-cec4-558b-83ce-0451e10c41da" :answer/id #uuid "330011e7-cec4-558b-83ce-0451e10c41da" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "4\sqrt{3}\,m/s" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-70c5036d-e847-5a0e-bf6c-48538005df98" :answer/id #uuid "70c5036d-e847-5a0e-bf6c-48538005df98" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "5\,m/s" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-7e188a6e-5859-50df-8694-4924096a1526" :answer/id #uuid "7e188a6e-5859-50df-8694-4924096a1526" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "7\,m/s" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-52f39f9c-16d0-5e71-b870-45274fd72ab1" :answer/id #uuid "52f39f9c-16d0-5e71-b870-45274fd72ab1" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\sqrt{55}\,m/s" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-dd5d7801-28ac-5ea0-88d2-5bd0cb858a80" :answer/id #uuid "dd5d7801-28ac-5ea0-88d2-5bd0cb858a80" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\sqrt{61}\,m/s" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186180703 :tutorial/content "We've seen how to calculate a particle's velocity and displacement when its acceleration is a function of *displacement.* In this lesson, we'll use this knowledge to compute various properties of a particle in motion.  

Suppose a particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis. Its displacement from the origin is $x\,\rm{m},$ its velocity is $v\,\rm{m/s},$ and its acceleration is $2x\,\rm{m/s}^2.$ 

![](images/52/5222b12a7f08a33dc981ac95bd717cce945e1d2e3565fb3631f108fd0f307a12.png)

Furthermore, suppose $P$ has velocity $2\,\rm{m/s}$ when its displacement is $\sqrt{3}\,\rm{m}.$ 

Let's use this information to determine at which values of $x$ the particle is instantaneously at rest.

Since the acceleration of the particle $P$ is $2x\,\rm{m/s}^2,$ we have

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}t} =2x.
$$

Using the fact that

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}t}= \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}v^2\right),
$$

we can rewrite our equation as

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}v^2\right) = 2x.
$$

Integrating both sides of the above equation with respect to $x,$ we have

$$
\int \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(\dfrac12v^2\right) \textrm{d}x
=
\int 2x \:\textrm{d}x
$$

which gives the general solution

$$
\dfrac12v^2 = x^2+ C.
$$

Now, since $v=2\,\rm{m/s}$ when $x=\sqrt 3\,\rm{m},$ we can find the value of the constant $C,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & ={x}^{2}+C \\ \frac{1}{2}(2)^{2} & =(\sqrt{3})^{2}+C \\ 2 & =3+C \\ C & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\dfrac12v^2 = x^2-1.
$$

Finally, the particle is instantaneously at rest when $v(x) = 0\,\rm{m/s}.$ We find the displacement of the particle when $P$ is instantaneously at rest by substituting $v=0$ in the equation above and solving for $x{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & ={x}^{2}-1 \\ \frac{1}{2}(0)^{2} & ={x}^{2}-1 \\ {x}^{2} & =1 \\ x & =\pm 1\,m\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186179847 :activity/expected-seconds 1200.0 :db/ensure [:activity/validate]} [:db/retract 17592186371071 :answer-field/choices 17592186371072] [:db/retract 17592186246762 :answer-field/choices 17592186246094] [:db/retract 17592186246762 :answer-field/choices 17592186246134] [:db/retract 17592186246762 :answer-field/choices 17592186246229] [:db/retract 17592186246762 :answer-field/choices 17592186244344] [:db/retract 17592186246762 :answer-field/choices 17592186245454] {:db/id 17592186119857 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-d77196fa-8d44-5cad-922e-bddbeed8f53e"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id 17592186119858 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-a78df4d7-9e4a-5ba6-b17f-e12077b05fb4"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id "question-a78df4d7-9e4a-5ba6-b17f-e12077b05fb4" :question/id #uuid "a78df4d7-9e4a-5ba6-b17f-e12077b05fb4" :question/math-academy-id "q-76325" :question/problem "The vectors ${a}_{1},$ ${a}_{2},$ and ${a}_{3}$ are given below. Determine whether $B=\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}.$ If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2},$ where ${a}_{3}={x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}.$

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$" :question/worked-solution "We want to determine if $B$ is indeed a basis of $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}.$ So, we want to find ${x}_{1},{x}_{2}\in R$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{1}}+{x}_{2}{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{2}}={{[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{3}}.
$$

This equation is equivalent to the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=5 \\ -{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=3\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we reduce the augmented matrix of the system to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 5 \\ -1 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the RREF matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st and $2$nd columns. So,  $B$ is indeed a basis of $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}.$
Also, the matrix tells us that ${x}_{1}=1$ and ${x}_{2}=4,$ meaning that

$$
1\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{1}}+4\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{2}}={{[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{3}}.
$$

Determine whether $B=\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3},{a}_{4}\}.$ If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3},$ where ${a}_{4}={x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}.$

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -9\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -8\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{4}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$" :question/worked-solution "We want to determine if $B$ is indeed a basis of $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3},{a}_{4}\}.$ So, we want to find ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}\in R$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -9\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{1}}+{x}_{2}{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{2}}+{x}_{3}{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -8\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{3}}={{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{4}}.
$$

This equation is equivalent to the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{3}=2 \\ -2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=-4 \\ -9{x}_{1}-8{x}_{3}=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we reduce the augmented matrix of the system to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 & -2 & -4 \\ -9 & 0 & -8 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -9 & 0 & -8 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+9{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 17\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & -15 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 17\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the reduced matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st, $2$nd, and $3$rd columns. So,  $B$ is indeed a basis of $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3},{a}_{4}\}.$
Also, the matrix tells us that ${x}_{1}=-15,$ ${x}_{2}=0,$ and ${x}_{3}=17,$ meaning that

$$
(-15)\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -9\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{1}}+0\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{2}}+17\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -8\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{3}}={{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{4}}.
$$

Therefore, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=(-15)+0+17=2.$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186371071 :answer-field/choices ["answer-684b58dc-c7bc-5e7a-ad38-d7e82bd7f00b"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-684b58dc-c7bc-5e7a-ad38-d7e82bd7f00b" :answer/id #uuid "684b58dc-c7bc-5e7a-ad38-d7e82bd7f00b" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "$\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ is not a basis of $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3},{a}_{4}\}$" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-d77196fa-8d44-5cad-922e-bddbeed8f53e" :question/id #uuid "d77196fa-8d44-5cad-922e-bddbeed8f53e" :question/math-academy-id "q-110851" :question/problem "Consider the vectors ${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],$ ${a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}],$ and ${a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}15 \\ 10 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$ Find a basis $B$ of $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}.$" :question/worked-solution "We need to find a subset of linearly independent vectors. :question/worked-solution "The number of infected files, $y(t),$ grows exponentially with a growth factor of $4.$

Let's write down what we know:

- $a = 10$ is the initial number of infected files

- $b = 4$ is the growth factor (the number of infected files quadruples)

- $t=$ the time (in hours)

The formula for exponential growth (in terms of a growth factor $b$) is

$$
y = ab^t.
$$

Therefore, the correct expression for $y(t)$ is

$$
y(t)= 10 \cdot 4^{t}.
$$

To find the number of files infected after $6$ hours, we  substitute $t=6$ into the above:

$$
y(6) = 10 \cdot 4^{6} = 40\,960
$$

Therefore, the computer will have $40\,960$ infected files after $6$ hours." :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186147474 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-a1c43e4b-f0c3-5827-a9fe-03d9f0ad0749" "question-3ef74434-74b6-5bd1-8d2d-3a97591fb1bc"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id 17592186147199 :question/problem "In the week of opening, the grocery store sold $20$ kilograms of apples. After that, the weekly sales increased by $25 \%$ every week. 

Find a function that models the total weight of apples sold in week $t$ after opening, and use this function to find the total amount of apples sold in the $4$th week." :question/worked-solution "The number of kilograms of apples sold $y(t)$ grows exponentially with a growth rate of $25 \%.$

Let's write down what we know:

- $a = 20$ is the total weight of the apples (in kilograms) sold initially

- $r = 0.25$ is the growth rate ($25 \%$ expressed as a decimal)

- $t=$ the time (in weeks) after opening

The formula for exponential growth (in terms of a growth rate $r$) is

$$
y = a(1+r)^t.
$$

Therefore, the correct expression for $y(t)$ is

$$
y   = 20 \cdot (1 + 0.25)^{t}.
$$

Simplifying the above, we get

$$
y(t) = 20 \cdot (1.25)^{t}.
$$

To find the total weight of apples sold in week $4,$ we evaluate the above for $t=4\mathbin{:}$

$$
y(4) = 20 \cdot (1.25)^{4} \approx 49
$$

Therefore, approximately $49$ kilograms of apples were sold in week $4.$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186147475 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-0f781a71-78ec-54be-875d-95c07fb380d7"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id 17592186147215 :question/worked-solution "The number of listeners $L(t)$ grows exponentially with a growth rate of $190\%.$

Let's write down what we know:

- $a = 80$ is the total number of listeners initially

- $r = 1.9$ is the growth rate ($190\%$ expressed as a decimal)

- $t=$ the time (in weeks) after release

The formula for exponential growth is

$$
L = a(1+r)^t.
$$

Therefore, the correct expression for $L(t)$ is

$$
L = 80 \cdot (1 + 1.9)^{t}.
$$

Simplifying the above, we get

$$
L(t) = 80 \cdot (2.9)^{t}.
$$

To find the total number of listeners after $2$ weeks, we evaluate the above for $t=2{:}$

$$
L(2) = 80 \cdot (2.9)^{2} \approx 673
$$

Therefore, the estimated number of listeners after $2$ weeks is $673.$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "question-a3269c43-47df-5acc-97bf-5a6fd7c5c99e" :question/id #uuid "a3269c43-47df-5acc-97bf-5a6fd7c5c99e" :question/math-academy-id "q-103103" :question/problem "The number of bacteria $y(t)$ in a culture after $t$ hours is given by the following formula:

An exponential model estimates that at the end of each week after launch, the number of students increased by $160%$ of the number of students at the end of the previous week.

Therefore, the estimated number of students after $3$ weeks is $1758.$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-9b4c7c93-453d-5bac-b606-f82c34cb377d"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-9b4c7c93-453d-5bac-b606-f82c34cb377d" :answer-field/id #uuid "9b4c7c93-453d-5bac-b606-f82c34cb377d" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-3ca45b50-aa83-548f-8093-7884f91372f8" :answer-field/choices ["answer-360767c6-d66d-5903-9180-b0da4415a5dc" "answer-bc6abb1b-3487-54e7-bdd5-09377dd6493c" "answer-3ca45b50-aa83-548f-8093-7884f91372f8" "answer-ad1a9c65-fa8c-5d77-8312-c62177840ed0" "answer-6d3bbde6-9914-5283-a9d6-322d06b9ef0b"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-360767c6-d66d-5903-9180-b0da4415a5dc" :answer/id #uuid "360767c6-d66d-5903-9180-b0da4415a5dc" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "1506" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-bc6abb1b-3487-54e7-bdd5-09377dd6493c" :answer/id #uuid "bc6abb1b-3487-54e7-bdd5-09377dd6493c" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "160" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-3ca45b50-aa83-548f-8093-7884f91372f8" :answer/id #uuid "3ca45b50-aa83-548f-8093-7884f91372f8" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "1758" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-ad1a9c65-fa8c-5d77-8312-c62177840ed0" :answer/id #uuid "ad1a9c65-fa8c-5d77-8312-c62177840ed0" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "1962" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-6d3bbde6-9914-5283-a9d6-322d06b9ef0b" :answer/id #uuid "6d3bbde6-9914-5283-a9d6-322d06b9ef0b" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "410" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186147767 :question/worked-solution "The number of views $V(t)$ grows exponentially with a growth rate of $250%.$

Therefore, the estimated number of views after $3$ hours is $3859.$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186144303 :answer-field/correct 17592186144304 :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id 17592186148684 :tutorial/content "Suppose that there are $120$ deer in a wildlife reserve. If the deer population doubles every year, can we find a function that gives the number of deer after $t$ years? 

First, let's write down what we know:

- $a = 120$ is the **initial number** of deer

- $b =2$ is the **growth factor** (equal to $2$ because the number of deer doubles every year)

- $t=$ the time (in years)

We let $y(t)$ be the number of deer in the reserve after $t$ years.  The formula for $y(t)$ is given by

$$
y(t) = ab^t.
$$

Substituting our values for $a$ and $b,$ we get

$$
y(t) = 120\cdot 2^t.
$$

We can use this formula to find the number of deer in the reserve for any value of $t \geq 0.$ For example, to find the number of deer after $3$ years, we substitute $t=3$ into the function:

$$
\begin{aligned}y(3) & =120\cdot {2}^{3} \\  & =120\cdot 8 \\  & =960\end{aligned}
$$

So there will be $960$ deer after $3$ years.

Finally, notice that substituting $t=0$ into the formula gives the initial number of deer:

$$
\begin{aligned}y(0) & =120\cdot {2}^{0} \\  & =120\cdot 1 \\  & =120\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186148683 :tutorial/content "When dealing with exponential growth, it's more common to be given a **growth rate** instead of a growth factor. A growth rate is usually expressed as a percent.

For example, suppose that an investor invests $\[math]500$ dollars in the shares of some high-growth companies. It's expected that the investment will grow by $35\%$ each year. Can we write a function that describes the value of the investment after $t$ years? 

Let's write down what we know:

- $a=\[/math]500$ is the **initial value** of the investment

- $r = 0.35$ is the **growth rate** (this is simply $35\%$ expressed as a decimal)

- $t$ is the time (in years)

Let $y(t)$ be the value of the investment after $t$ years. The formula for $y(t)$ is given by

$$
y = a(1+r)^t.
$$

Substituting in our values for $a$ and $r,$ we get

$$
y(t) = 500(1+0.35)^t.
$$

Simplifying the above, we arrive at

$$
y(t) = 500(1.35)^t.
$$

When creating exponential growth functions, the key takeaway is this:

- If you're given a **growth rate** $r$ (usually expressed as a percent), then use the formula $y = a(1+r)^t.$

- If you're given a **growth factor** $b,$ then use the formula $y = ab^t.$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186147671 :activity/expected-seconds 420.0 :db/ensure [:activity/validate]} {:db/id 17592186064305 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-180b64b1-b15e-57ee-9a92-ff79a509bb19" "question-f02573a0-2790-58d2-b6cc-7bac38c415b0" "question-7c4e2820-92a5-519d-9225-25cc4948f0c9"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id "question-180b64b1-b15e-57ee-9a92-ff79a509bb19" :question/id #uuid "180b64b1-b15e-57ee-9a92-ff79a509bb19" :question/math-academy-id "q-129431" :question/problem "$\sqrt{{a}^{2}{b}^{2}}=$" :question/worked-solution "Remember that the square root of a perfect square can be simplified using absolute value.

$$
\sqrt{{x}^{2}}=|x|
$$

Also, we notice that ${a}^{2}$ and ${b}^{2}$ are perfect squares.

First, we write the expression under the square root as a perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{{a}^{2}{b}^{2}} & =\sqrt{a\cdot a\cdot b\cdot b} \\  & =\sqrt{a\cdot b\cdot a\cdot b} \\  & =\sqrt{(ab)\cdot (ab)} \\  & =\sqrt{(ab)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we take the absolute value of the squared quantity:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{(ab)^{2}} & =|ab|\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-e9a1e499-9cd1-5d15-a079-6c7d6a1a34e4"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-e9a1e499-9cd1-5d15-a079-6c7d6a1a34e4" :answer-field/id #uuid "e9a1e499-9cd1-5d15-a079-6c7d6a1a34e4" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-a8914752-237a-5f09-b64c-97f60b10586b" :answer-field/choices ["answer-1aec2d0b-0038-5b9d-8e4f-821e3fd956b9" "answer-677e43b4-9e76-52a3-a1bb-1004c237476a" "answer-99522d80-934c-58f8-8645-3e3d69f47b0b" "answer-a8914752-237a-5f09-b64c-97f60b10586b" "answer-9f014637-b6bb-5d87-a79d-711ebb7c4222"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-1aec2d0b-0038-5b9d-8e4f-821e3fd956b9" :answer/id #uuid "1aec2d0b-0038-5b9d-8e4f-821e3fd956b9" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\pm ab" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-677e43b4-9e76-52a3-a1bb-1004c237476a" :answer/id #uuid "677e43b4-9e76-52a3-a1bb-1004c237476a" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "ab" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-99522d80-934c-58f8-8645-3e3d69f47b0b" :answer/id #uuid "99522d80-934c-58f8-8645-3e3d69f47b0b" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "a|b|" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-a8914752-237a-5f09-b64c-97f60b10586b" :answer/id #uuid "a8914752-237a-5f09-b64c-97f60b10586b" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "|ab|" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-9f014637-b6bb-5d87-a79d-711ebb7c4222" :answer/id #uuid "9f014637-b6bb-5d87-a79d-711ebb7c4222" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "|a|b" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-f02573a0-2790-58d2-b6cc-7bac38c415b0" :question/id #uuid "f02573a0-2790-58d2-b6cc-7bac38c415b0" :question/math-academy-id "q-129432" :question/problem "$\sqrt{{y}^{2}{z}^{2}}=$" :question/worked-solution "Remember that the square root of a perfect square can be simplified using absolute value.

$$
\sqrt{{x}^{2}}=|x|
$$

Also, we notice that ${y}^{2}$ and ${z}^{2}$ are perfect squares.

First, we write the expression under the square root as a perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{{y}^{2}{z}^{2}} & =\sqrt{y\cdot y\cdot z\cdot z} \\  & =\sqrt{y\cdot z\cdot y\cdot z} \\  & =\sqrt{(yz)\cdot (yz)} \\  & =\sqrt{(yz)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we take the absolute value of the squared quantity:

How many square kilometers does the area increase by between day $1$ and day $2?$" :question/worked-solution "To find the growth of the patch between day $1$ and day $2$, we need to subtract the area after day $1$ from the area after day $2.$ So we need to calculate

$$
A(2)-A(1).
$$

First, we find the area after the first day, $A(1)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}A(1) & =10\cdot (1.1)^{1} \\  & =10\cdot 1.1 \\  & =11\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find $A(2),$ the area after the second day:

$$
\begin{aligned}A(2) & =10\cdot (1.1)^{2} \\  & =10\cdot 1.21 \\  & =12.1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the growth of the patch between day $1$ and day $2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A(2)-A(1) & =12.1-11=1.1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the area increased by $1.1$ square kilometer between day $1$ and day $2.$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard :question/answer-fields $$
M(3)-M(2).
$$

First, we find the population after the second year, $M(2)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}M(2) & =1\,000\cdot (1.6)^{(2)} \\  & =1\,000\cdot 2.56 \\  & =2\,560\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find $M(3),$ the population after the third year:

$$
\begin{aligned}M(3) & =1\,000\cdot (1.6)^{(3)} \\  & =1\,000\cdot 4.096 \\  & =4\,096\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the growth in the population between year $2$ and year $3$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}M(3)-M(2) & =4\,096-2\,560=1\,536.\end{aligned}
$$

The given expression is an exponential growth expression of the form $y(t)=a\cdot (1+r)^{t}$, where:

- $a=800$ represents the initial area covered by the  blueberry bushes

- $1+r=1.1,$ where $r$ is the growth rate

- $t$ is the number of years since $2015$

Solving for $r$:

$$
1+r=1.1\,⟹\,r=0.1
$$

Now, $0.1$ (expressed as a percent) is equal to $10%.$ Therefore, the area covered by the bushes grows at a rate of $10%$ per year." :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard ["question-fd9f0c45-62d6-5bab-b897-93c9f4793a8e" "question-42308119-ffcd-55c6-b052-68e017e7cc90"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id 17592186162529 :question/problem "Consider the set $A,$ defined as

$$
A=\{\frac{(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}+1}:n\in \{1,2,3,4\}\}.
$$

What is the supremum of $A?$

$sup(A)=$
{{field-1}}" :question/worked-solution "The supremum of a set $A$ is the smallest upper bound of $A.$

If $A$ is a finite set, the supremum of $A$ equals its maximum. 

First, let's write down all the terms of our set by substituting $n=1,2,3,4$ into the expression for the elements of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(-1)^{1}}{(1)^{2}+1} & =-\frac{1}{2} \\ \frac{(-1)^{2}}{(2)^{2}+1} & =\frac{1}{5} \\ \frac{(-1)^{3}}{(3)^{2}+1} & =-\frac{1}{10} \\ \frac{(-1)^{4}}{(4)^{2}+1} & =\frac{1}{17}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
A=\{-\frac{1}{2},\,\frac{1}{5},\,-\frac{1}{10},\,\frac{1}{17}\}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}sup(A) & =max\{-\frac{1}{2},\,\frac{1}{5},\,-\frac{1}{10},\,\frac{1}{17}\}=\frac{1}{5}.\end{aligned}

"03070e45-f0e3-5991-b98c-709745709961" :question/math-academy-id "q-253526" :question/problem "Consider the following set.

$$
A=\{7-{(\frac{1}{2})}^{n}\,:\,n\in N\}

For this set, we have {{field-1}}." :question/worked-solution "The supremum of a set $A$ is the smallest upper bound of $A.$

To find the supremum of this set, we must find the set containing **all** upper bounds of $A$ (i.e., the set of upper bounds) and take the minimum of this set.

The elements of $A$ are all the terms of the sequence ${a}_{n},$ given by

$$
{a}_{n}=7-{(\frac{1}{2})}^{n},\,n\in N=\{1,2,3,4,…\}.
$$

Let's draw some points of our sequence on the real line:

![](images/ca/cae6f56db55b49b98df6ce7e3ae0777e725af14de9dedb5b61b54039bac41860.png)

We see that ${a}_{n}$ is increasing and converges to $7.$ 

So, in our case, we have that

- any number in the set $x\ge 7$ is an upper bound of $A,$

- any number in the set $x<7$ is **not** an upper bound of $A.$ In other words, we can always find a sufficiently large $n$ so that $7-{(\frac{1}{2})}^{n}$ is greater than $x$ for any $x<7.$

Therefore, $[7,\infty )$ is the set of upper bounds of $A,$ and 

$$
sup(A)=min[7,\infty )=7.
$$

Notice that $7$ is *not* the maximum of $A$ (the set $A$ has no maximum). Therefore, we conclude that

For this set, we have that {{field-1}}." :question/worked-solution "The supremum of a set $A$ is the smallest upper bound of $A.$

To find the supremum of this set, we must find the set containing **all** upper bounds of $A$ (i.e., the set of upper bounds) and take the minimum of this set.

The elements of $A$ are the terms of the sequence ${a}_{n},$ given by

$$
{a}_{n}=3+2{(\frac{3}{5})}^{n},\,n\in N=\{1,2,3,4,…\}.
$$

Let's draw some points of our sequence on the real line:

![](images/05/05737c6e8e7b88f1a91a5fd6cc7d5b6a088227e327ef66e937e279c090a47256.png)

We see that ${a}_{n}$ is decreasing and converges to $3.$ The maximum of $A$ is 

$$
max(A)={a}_{1}=3+2{(\frac{3}{5})}^{1}=\frac{21}{5}.
$$

So, in our case, we have that

- any number $x\ge {a}_{1}$ is an upper bound of $A,$

- any number $x<{a}_{1}$ cannot be an upper bound because ${a}_{1},$ an element of $A,$ is greater than $x.$

Therefore, $[\frac{21}{5},\infty )$ is the set of upper bounds of $A,$ and 

$$
sup(A)=min[\frac{21}{5},\infty )=\frac{21}{5}.
$$

Notice that $\frac{21}{5}$ is the maximum of $A.$ Therefore, we conclude that

$$
sup(A)=\frac{21}{5}\in A.
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-f7ca4c4c-da25-5075-bde9-61051e330507"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id To find the supremum of a set $A,$ we must find the set containing **all** upper bounds of $A$ (i.e., the set of upper bounds) and take the minimum of this set.

- any number $y\ge 4$ is an upper bound of $A,$

- any number $y<4$ cannot be an upper bound of $A$ because $4,$ an element of $A,$ is greater than $y.$

$$
{sup}_{x\in R}f(x)=sup(A)=min[4,\infty )=4.

We start by drawing up our synthetic division table:

$$
\begin{aligned} & x & {x}^{0} \\ 3 & 6 & 5 \\  & ↓ & 18 \\  & 6 & 23\end{aligned}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\frac{6x+5}{x-3}=6+\frac{23}{x-3}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{6x+5}{x-3}\,\text{d}x & =\int (6+\frac{23}{x-3})\text{d}x \\  & =6\int \text{d}x+23\int \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =6x+23\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|+C.\end{aligned}

$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-39ab24d6-268c-5219-a363-1c64d249620f" "answer-field-728aa6ab-95a5-58ca-8540-251eb130c4b8"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-39ab24d6-268c-5219-a363-1c64d249620f" :answer-field/id #uuid "39ab24d6-268c-5219-a363-1c64d249620f" :answer-field/key "field-1" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank :answer-field/correct "answer-6613762c-3532-5365-82fc-bc7a05901a9e" :answer-field/choices ["answer-6613762c-3532-5365-82fc-bc7a05901a9e"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-6613762c-3532-5365-82fc-bc7a05901a9e" :answer/id #uuid "6613762c-3532-5365-82fc-bc7a05901a9e" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "14" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-728aa6ab-95a5-58ca-8540-251eb130c4b8" :answer-field/id #uuid "728aa6ab-95a5-58ca-8540-251eb130c4b8" :answer-field/key "field-2" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank :answer-field/correct "answer-d5c32443-63e9-5fe5-8cce-5815205faa9d" :answer-field/choices ["answer-d5c32443-63e9-5fe5-8cce-5815205faa9d"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-d5c32443-63e9-5fe5-8cce-5815205faa9d" :answer/id #uuid "d5c32443-63e9-5fe5-8cce-5815205faa9d" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{5}{3}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-6e5fb422-3b84-5ae8-83c2-850e3c9cae23" :question/id #uuid "6e5fb422-3b84-5ae8-83c2-850e3c9cae23" :question/math-academy-id "q-352242" :question/problem "Evaluate the following integral:

{{field-1}} $-\,4\operatorname{ln}⁡(${{field-2}}$)$" :question/worked-solution "The denominator of the integrand doesn't divide the numerator exactly, so we need to decompose it into its quotient and remainder. For this, we can use synthetic division.

We start by drawing up our synthetic division table:

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

|  | $↓$ | $-3$ | $-9$ |

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+6x+5}{x+3}=x+3-\frac{4}{x+3}.

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{{x}^{2}+6x+5}{x+3}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(x+3-\frac{4}{x+3})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}x\,\text{d}x+3{\int }_{0}^{2}\text{d}x-4{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{x+3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}\,{|}_{0}^{2}+3x\,{|}_{0}^{2}-4\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+3|\,{|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({2}^{2}-{0}^{2})+3(2-0)-4(\operatorname{ln}⁡|2+3|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|0+3|) \\  & =2+6-4(\operatorname{ln}⁡5-\operatorname{ln}⁡3) \\  & =8-4\operatorname{ln}⁡(\,\frac{5}{3}\,).\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-17c83049-3bba-5626-8130-3871dbe37307" "answer-field-76fddc9d-060b-5c62-80a7-51c466e021a5"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-17c83049-3bba-5626-8130-3871dbe37307" :answer-field/id #uuid "17c83049-3bba-5626-8130-3871dbe37307" :answer-field/key "field-1" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank :answer-field/correct "answer-971e21a4-35f1-5a29-ba6e-cbf260b798f3" :answer-field/choices ["answer-971e21a4-35f1-5a29-ba6e-cbf260b798f3"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-971e21a4-35f1-5a29-ba6e-cbf260b798f3" :answer/id #uuid "971e21a4-35f1-5a29-ba6e-cbf260b798f3" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "8" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-76fddc9d-060b-5c62-80a7-51c466e021a5" :answer-field/id #uuid "76fddc9d-060b-5c62-80a7-51c466e021a5" :answer-field/key "field-2" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank :answer-field/correct "answer-198fdf6b-a075-5de2-8b17-668c98530091" :answer-field/choices ["answer-198fdf6b-a075-5de2-8b17-668c98530091"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-198fdf6b-a075-5de2-8b17-668c98530091" :answer/id #uuid "198fdf6b-a075-5de2-8b17-668c98530091" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{5}{3}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-8c284bd6-ffb5-522e-9bbf-08c92df09daa" :question/id #uuid "8c284bd6-ffb5-522e-9bbf-08c92df09daa" :question/math-academy-id "q-347424" :question/problem "Evaluate the following integral:

{{field-2}} $)$" :question/worked-solution "First, we pull out the factor of $3$ from the denominator:

Then, we draw up our synthetic division table to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder.

|  | ${x}^{1}$ | ${x}^{0}$ |

$$

Therefore,

$$

We need to write the integrand so that it's something we can integrate. One way to do this is to divide $3x+2$ by $x+2$ using polynomial or synthetic division. We'll use synthetic division because it's faster. 

To rewrite $\dfrac{3x+2}{x+2},$ we complete a synthetic division table.

|  | $x^1$ | $x^0$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\color{red}-2$ | $3$ | $2$ |
|  | $\color{gray}\downarrow$ | $-6$ |
|  | $3$ | $-4$ |

This tells us that $\dfrac{3x+2}{x+2}$ can be decomposed into a quotient and remainder as

$$
\dfrac{3x+2}{x+2}= 3 - \dfrac{4}{x+2}.
$$

Now, we can integrate the function, which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3x+2}{x+2}\,\text{d}x & =\int (3-\frac{4}{x+2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int 3\,\text{d}x-4\int \frac{1}{x+2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3x-4\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+2|+C.\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186064429 :activity/expected-seconds 1080.0 :db/ensure [:activity/validate]} {:db/id 17592186065096 :step/math-academy-id 630729 :db/ensure [:step/validate]} {:db/id 17592186065102 :step/math-academy-id 630730 :db/ensure [:step/validate]} {:db/id 17592186065103 :step/math-academy-id 630733 :db/ensure [:step/validate]} {:db/id 17592186065113 :step/math-academy-id 630736 :db/ensure [:step/validate]} {:db/id 17592186326788 :question/problem "Find the acute angle between the vector $x$ and the subspace spanned by the linearly independent vectors $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\},$ where

$$

:question/problem "Suppose that the function $f(x,y)$ and all of its first and second-order partial derivatives are continuous on an open set $U.$ Which of the following pairs could represent the first-order partial derivatives of $f(x,y)?$

I. ${f}_{x}(x,y)=y{x}^{2}-4y$ and ${f}_{y}(x,y)=\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}-4x$

II. ${f}_{x}(x,y)=3-5x$ and ${f}_{y}(x,y)=1$

III. ${f}_{x}(x,y)=3{x}^{2}+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y$ and ${f}_{y}(x,y)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y-2{y}^{3}{e}^{{y}^{2}}$" :question/worked-solution "Since the function and its first and second-order partial derivatives are continuous on an open set $U,$ the mixed partial derivatives must be equal, that is, ${f}_{xy}(x,y)={f}_{yx}(x,y).$ Let's check if this condition is true for each of our pairs of first-order partial derivatives.

- For the first pair, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y{x}^{2}-4y)={x}^{2}-4 \\ {f}_{yx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}-4x)={x}^{2}-4.\end{aligned}
$$

As ${f}_{xy}(x,y)={f}_{yx}(x,y)$, the first pair could represent the first-order partial derivatives of $f(x,y).$

- For the second pair, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(3-5x)=0 \\ {f}_{yx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(1)=0.\end{aligned}
$$

As ${f}_{xy}(x,y)={f}_{yx}(x,y)$, the second pair could represent the first-order partial derivatives of $f(x,y).$

- For the third pair, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(3{x}^{2}+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y) \\  & =0+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡y \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y \\ {f}_{yx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y-2{y}^{3}{e}^{{y}^{2}}) \\  & =(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡y-0 \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y.\end{aligned}
$$

As ${f}_{xy}(x,y)\ne {f}_{yx}(x,y)$,  the third pair cannot represent the first-order partial derivatives of $f(x,y).$

Therefore, the correct answer is 'I and II only'." :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-df0c4030-39f2-5bc9-a0e8-ac2b199792a8"] :db/ensure 17592186054399 :question/problem "What is the solution to $7z \lt -21?$" :question/worked-solution "The variable $z$ is being *multiplied* by $7.$ To isolate $z$, we perform the *opposite* operation, which is *dividing* by $7.$ Remember to perform the same operation on both sides.

$$
\begin{aligned}7z & <-21 \\ \frac{7z}{7} & <\frac{-21}{7} \\ \frac{7z}{7} & <-3\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can cancel a common factor of $7$ from the numerator and denominator.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{7z}{7} & <-3 \\ \frac{\cancel{7}z}{\cancel{7}} & <-3 \\ z & <-3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $z \lt -3.$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186054770 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-eadfd460-afeb-5be8-ba9d-32eedcec4158" "question-cf24a3ad-fa5d-5add-9240-16d745dab1cc" "question-9c17e0c0-dc11-5aeb-b1ca-6cfde8f72eed" "question-e481e652-2dec-5a50-9597-483a3ddecf5c"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id 17592186054400 :question/problem "Solve the inequality $-6x \leq -7 .$" :question/worked-solution "The variable $x$ is being *multiplied* by $-6.$ To isolate $x,$ we perform the *opposite* operation, which is *dividing* by $-6.$ Remember to perform the same operation on both sides.

Also, when multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

$$
\begin{aligned}-6x\,\, & \le \,\,-7 \\ \frac{-6x}{-6}\,\, & \ge \,\,\frac{-7}{-6} \\ \frac{-6x}{-6}\,\, & \ge \,\,\frac{7}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can cancel a common factor of $-6$ from both the numerator and denominator.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-6x}{-6} & \ge \frac{7}{6} \\ \frac{\cancel{-6}x}{\cancel{-6}} & \ge \frac{7}{6} \\ x & \ge \frac{7}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x \geq \dfrac{7}{6}.$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186054771 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-24cf9a94-daed-5188-bbde-60124c7a3e18" "question-2c5ad69f-c453-5e7c-98b1-f37e29e67532"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id 17592186054401 :question/problem "Solve the inequality $-\dfrac{y}{8} \leq -4.$" :question/worked-solution "The variable $y$ is being *divided* by $8.$ To isolate $y$ and remove the negative sign, we *multiply* by $-8.$ 

Remember, when multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{y}{8}\,\, & \le \,\,-4 \\ (-8)\cdot (-\frac{y}{8})\,\, & \ge \,\,(-8)\cdot (-4) \\ (-8)\cdot (-\frac{y}{8})\,\, & \ge \,\,32\end{aligned}
$$

Since two negative numbers multiply to give a positive number, we first cancel the negatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}(-8)\cdot (-\frac{y}{8}) & \ge 32 \\ (\cancel{-}8)\cdot (\cancel{-}\frac{y}{8}) & \ge 32 \\ 8\cdot \frac{y}{8} & \ge 32\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can cancel a common factor of $8$ from both the numerator and denominator.

$$
\begin{aligned}8\cdot \frac{y}{8} & \ge 32 \\ \frac{8y}{8} & \ge 32 \\ \frac{\cancel{8}y}{\cancel{8}} & \ge 32 \\ y & \ge 32\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $y \geq 32.$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186054772 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-1c83e356-5c28-5a7c-9e2e-dbd984ca824b"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id 17592186054402 :question/problem "Solve the inequality $-9 \leq -3z.$" :question/worked-solution "The variable $z$ is being *multiplied* by $-3.$ To isolate $z,$ we can perform the *opposite* operation, which is *dividing* by $-3.$ Remember to perform the same operation on both sides.

Also, when multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

$$
\begin{aligned}-9\,\, & \le \,\,-3z \\ \frac{-9}{-3}\,\, & \ge \,\,\frac{-3z}{-3} \\ 3\,\, & \ge \,\,\frac{-3z}{-3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can cancel the common factor $-3$ from both the numerator and denominator.

$$
\begin{aligned}3 & \ge \frac{-3z}{-3} \\ 3 & \ge \frac{\cancel{-3}z}{\cancel{-3}} \\ 3 & \ge z\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we rewrite the inequality with the variable on the left-hand side:

$$
z \leq 3
$$

Therefore, the solution is $z \leq 3.$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "question-a32936a3-d0e7-5359-880f-a816d9cf59f9" :question/id #uuid "a32936a3-d0e7-5359-880f-a816d9cf59f9" :question/math-academy-id "q-153998" :question/problem "What is the solution to $6z>-5?$" :question/worked-solution "The variable $z$ is being *multiplied* by $6.$ To isolate $z,$ we perform the *opposite* operation, which is *dividing* by $6.$ Remember to perform the same operation on both sides.

Remember, when multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{y}{3}\,\, & \le \,\,4 \\ (-3)\cdot (-\frac{y}{3})\,\, & \ge \,\,(-3)\cdot 4 \\ (-3)\cdot (-\frac{y}{3})\,\, & \ge \,\,-12\end{aligned}
$$

Since two negative numbers multiply to give a positive number, we first cancel the negatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}(-3)\cdot (-\frac{y}{3})\,\, & \ge -12 \\ (\cancel{-}3)\cdot (\cancel{-}\frac{y}{3}) & \ge -12 \\ 3\cdot \frac{y}{3} & \ge -12\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can cancel a common factor of $3$ from both the numerator and denominator.

$$
\begin{aligned}3\cdot \frac{y}{3} & \ge -12 \\ \frac{3y}{3} & \ge -12 \\ \frac{\cancel{3}y}{\cancel{3}} & \ge -12 \\ y & \ge -12\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $y\ge -12.$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-9febe4e4-9bba-517f-959d-bd5f66e0861c" "answer-field-e9f64c01-1af9-5569-9108-05d2c71dd293"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-9febe4e4-9bba-517f-959d-bd5f66e0861c" :answer-field/id #uuid "9febe4e4-9bba-517f-959d-bd5f66e0861c" :answer-field/key "field-1" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank :answer-field/correct "answer-37fd20a8-7d5e-59b1-a20f-b74ee738720b" :answer-field/choices ["answer-37fd20a8-7d5e-59b1-a20f-b74ee738720b"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-37fd20a8-7d5e-59b1-a20f-b74ee738720b" :answer/id #uuid "37fd20a8-7d5e-59b1-a20f-b74ee738720b" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\ge" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-e9f64c01-1af9-5569-9108-05d2c71dd293" :answer-field/id #uuid "e9f64c01-1af9-5569-9108-05d2c71dd293" :answer-field/key "field-2" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank :answer-field/correct "answer-b4a8742a-2daa-546c-b4d9-fbc8f9111dcd" :answer-field/choices ["answer-b4a8742a-2daa-546c-b4d9-fbc8f9111dcd"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-b4a8742a-2daa-546c-b4d9-fbc8f9111dcd" :answer/id #uuid "b4a8742a-2daa-546c-b4d9-fbc8f9111dcd" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-12" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-2c5ad69f-c453-5e7c-98b1-f37e29e67532" :question/id #uuid "2c5ad69f-c453-5e7c-98b1-f37e29e67532" :question/math-academy-id "q-154011" :question/problem "Solve the inequality $-\frac{y}{4}\ge -8.$" :question/worked-solution "The variable $y$ is being *divided* by $4.$ To isolate $y$ and remove the negative sign, we *multiply* by $-4.$

is $y${{field-1}}{{field-2}}." :question/worked-solution "The variable $y$ is being *multiplied* by $6.$ To isolate $y,$ we perform the *opposite* operation, which is *dividing* by $6.$ Remember to
